observations.claim: The SOS countdown sheet cancels the emergency on any incidental dismissal — swipe-down, scrim tap, or system back all route to onCancel with no confirmation.
observations.evidence: SosBottomSheet.kt:34 `ModalBottomSheet(onDismissRequest = onCancel, ...)`; LiveTrackingScreen.kt:152 wires onCancel to `sosViewModel.onCancelCountdown()`. No ModalBottomSheetProperties(shouldDismissOnBackPress=false) and no confirm-to-cancel step. A phone jostled in a pocket or bag during the 30-second window silently aborts the alert and the user is given no notification that it was aborted.

observations.claim: SOS takes 30 seconds to fire, which is presented as the default path with no immediate-send option that skips confirmation.
observations.evidence: SosViewModel.kt:114-118 `for (sec in 30 downTo 1) { _sosUiState.value = SosUiState.Countdown(sec); delay(1_000L) }`. The only way to shorten it is to find and tap 'Send now' (SosBottomSheet.kt:59-63) — i.e. two deliberate taps on a screen the user must first reach. For a distress control this is a long unassisted window.

observations.claim: The emergency-send action carries brand-primary styling, not danger styling, and is visually a peer of the cancel action.
observations.evidence: SosBottomSheet.kt:59-69 stacks HsPrimaryButton (filled, brand primary — HsComponents.kt:41-47 uses bare M3 Button with theme colors) directly above HsSecondaryButton, both fillMaxWidth. The only red on the sheet is the countdown numeral (SosBottomSheet.kt:48). Under panic + sunlight, two stacked full-width buttons with no colour differentiation on the destructive/urgent axis is a mis-tap generator.

observations.claim: The evidence-upload error sheet throws away the real error and cannot be retried.
